significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the conclusion that “a student's OWN per-token surprise under its single teacher is a sufficient proxy” for carrier tokens, that suppressing their gradients reduces trait transmission, and that “restricting the regularizer to early layers suffices”; P1 is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between measurable surprise and divergence-token status, while P2 and P3 are causal claims. It establishes both a phenomenon—a surprise-conditioned regularity across transmitted traits—and a mechanism linking sparse token gradients and early-layer changes to transmission, fixing expectations about which tokens carry traits and where preventive intervention should act. Cloud et al.'s “Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data” reports that semantic filtering does not remove transmission, so settling this specific trait-agnostic carrier signal would constrain a live defense bottleneck; the negative branches determinately reject surprise rather than rarity, gradient suppression, or early-layer sufficiency, although they would not rule out richer single-teacher signals. In the topic-substitution check, merely replacing these specifics with “extend subliminal learning” would not support this score; the independently measurable proxy-mechanism coupling is the claim-specific increment over the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handle is “Divergence-Token Regularization (DTR),” comprising the measurable surprise score “s_i = -log p_teacher(x_i | context)” and either gradient down-weighting or an early-layer consistency intervention; it is ex ante because it acts during training before the resulting student exhibits the transmitted trait. Since the hypothesis asserts that high-surprise rank predicts oracle divergence-token status and that a single shared threshold can suppress multiple traits, re-extraction on another model should recover a predicted relation rather than merely provide an unconstrained search procedure, although the asserted scope is limited to single-teacher distillation and may not survive adaptive teachers encoding traits in high-probability tokens. The downstream users include practitioners distilling from third-party teachers, who could insert the claimed “training-time immunization” before deployment, so the action window and uptake extend beyond researchers conducting post-hoc mechanistic analysis. Under topic substitution, subliminal learning alone supplies neither this screening quantity nor a preventive training knob; the score comes from the specific transferable, pre-outcome handle.
